discovery: Trapping and precision measurement of antimatter for tests of fundamental symmetries
subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / precision measurement
motivation: Gabrielse pioneered the capture, cooling and storage of antiprotons in Penning traps, the antiproton-to-proton charge-to-mass comparison, and the production of cold antihydrogen. With one-electron quantum cyclotron techniques he also measured the electron magnetic moment to 0.1 parts per trillion, the most stringent test of QED. Hangst's ALPHA collaboration achieved the first trapping of antihydrogen atoms (2010-2011), then precision laser spectroscopy of its 1S-2S transition at the 10^-12 level, hyperfine and Lamb-shift measurements, laser cooling of antihydrogen, and the first observation of antimatter's gravitational response (2023). Together these achievements have turned antimatter from an exotic species into a laboratory object studied with the precision of atomic physics. They provide the sharpest direct tests of CPT symmetry and the weak equivalence principle for antimatter, which bear on the cosmic matter-antimatter asymmetry. Their work rests on decades of patient, ingenious instrumentation.
